title: TOWARDS UNDERSTANDING THE SAFETY BOUNDARIES OF DEEPSEEK MODELS: EVALUATION AND FINDINGS
findings: The models were evaluated for 'Faith discrimination'. The attack success rates (ASRs) varied significantly by model and language. The DeepSeek-R1 model in English showed a particularly high ASR of over 50% for faith discrimination, which was substantially higher than its ASR in Chinese (around 25%) and also higher than the DeepSeek-V3 model in either language. This indicates a notable vulnerability to generating faith-based discriminatory content, especially for the DeepSeek-R1 model when prompted in English.
